summary: Describes the AM domain as the official Internet top-level domain of Armenia. It is an informational note about that country-code domain.

plainLanguage.summary: Every country has an internet ending, like a street suffix. This note is about the ending for Armenia.

subtitle: The Internet country-code top-level domain for the Republic of Armenia.

tldr.problem: Armenia needed an official Internet domain under which its organizations could register names.
tldr.mechanism: The .AM domain is assigned as Armenia's country-code top-level domain using the ISO 3166 2-letter country code. It uses a flat hierarchy where organizations register directly, with optional subdomains like .org.am.
tldr.outcome: Provides Armenia's Internet namespace, administered by the AM Network Information Center.

today: The .AM domain remains the official top-level domain for Armenia and continues to be administered by the AM Network Information Center.

sections.title: Armenia's Internet Domain
sections.content:
The .AM domain is the official top-level domain for the Republic of Armenia, based on its ISO 3166 two-letter country code. Like all country-code domains, it is registered with InterNIC and delegated to the country's network authorities.

The AM Network Information Center, Armenia's national Internet registry, administers the .AM domain and handles all registrations for Armenian organizations and citizens.
sections.plainLanguage: The .AM domain is the Internet address ending for Armenia, just like .US is for the United States.

sections.title: Naming Structure
sections.content:
The .AM domain uses a flat hierarchy, meaning any organization can register a domain name directly under .am (for example, arminco.am). However, subdomains are also permitted, such as .org.am, .co.am, .ac.am and .mil.am.

Two domains are reserved by the Armenian government: mil.am (Ministry of Defense) and gov.am (Government of Armenia). Other domains may be reserved for appropriate organizations by contacting the AM Network Information Center.
sections.plainLanguage: Armenian websites can end in .am, or in more specific endings like .org.am for organizations or .gov.am for government.

sections.title: Registration Process
sections.content:
Two types of registration are available: Delegation, where an organization runs its own name servers to manage a branch of the .AM domain, and Direct Registration, where information is stored in the AM Network Information Center's main database.

Direct registration can be for IP hosts (with an assigned IP address) or non-IP hosts (such as UUCP hosts). Applicants request a registration template from HOSTMASTER@AMNIC.NET, fill it out with their information, and submit it for consideration. More details are available at the AM Network Information Center website.
sections.plainLanguage: To get an .am domain, you fill out a form and send it to the AM Network Information Center. They might let you run your own name servers, or they can keep your information for you.
